intro: Oklahoma runs elections county by county, through the county election boards, with the State Election Board overseeing the state.

id_rule.text: Show a photo ID issued by the U.S. government, the State of Oklahoma, or a federally recognized tribe, with an expiration date after the election. You can also use the free voter ID card from your county election board. If you have neither, you can vote a provisional ballot and sign a sworn affidavit.

dates.detail: This is the voter registration deadline for the Nov. 3 election.

dates.label: Last day to request an absentee ballot
dates.detail: Your county election board must receive your request by 5 pm on this day.

src.label: Oklahoma State Election Board, absentee voting

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Vote at your county's early voting site. Hours are 8 am to 6 pm Wednesday to Friday and 8 am to 2 pm on Saturday. You must vote in the county where you are registered.

src.label: Oklahoma State Election Board, early voting

dates.label: Hand-delivered absentee ballots due
dates.detail: A hand-delivered absentee ballot must reach your county election board by the close of business on this Monday.

src.label: Oklahoma State Election Board, absentee voting

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 7 pm. A mailed absentee ballot must be received by your county election board by 7 pm.
